stories.headline: OpenAI's unreleased cyber model built 948 Linux root exploits and patches for $1.2M in one run

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published on Nov 4 an autonomous pipeline that, in one mid-October run with an upcoming, unnamed cyber model, produced working exploits and patches for 948 unique Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) bugs for $1,213,430 in API credits, or $1,279 each.
key_facts.excerpt: In a run in mid-October 2026, our pipeline using an upcoming cyber model dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and generated PoCs for 291 information leak vulnerabilities and 948 working local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits for a commonly used Linux distribution. The total run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, or $1,279 per LPE exploit.

key_facts.fact: The pipeline identified 2,308 candidate findings and reproduced 1,724 of them (about 74.7%) within 30 hours; human researchers reviewed exploits and patches before reporting to maintainers.
key_facts.excerpt: Within 30 hours, our system reproduced 1724 vulnerabilities, ~74.7% of the 2,308 candidate findings.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the newer model discovered more than 5x as many novel LPEs as a July run with GPT-5.6 Sol, despite three months of hardening between the scans.
key_facts.excerpt: Our analysis pipeline using the newer cyber model in mid-October discovered >5x more novel LPEs than a GPT-5.6 Sol run in July, despite three months of hardening between the scans.

key_facts.fact: The late-July comparison run with GPT-5.6 Sol found 166 unique LPEs for $513,690.
key_facts.excerpt: A late-July run with GPT-5.6 Sol found 166 unique LPEs for $513,690.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI values the 948 exploits at a hypothetical $18.9M to $66.3M using historical Pwn2Own ($20,000) and TyphoonPWN ($70,000) bounties, about 16x to 55x the pipeline's cost; targets ran a stock desktop OS, not a weakened one.
key_facts.excerpt: Applying those historical bounty amounts to the 948 exploits produces a hypothetical valuation of $18.9M—$66.3M, approximately 16x to 55x our pipeline's cost.

key_facts.fact: On Google's hardened kernelCTF target, the pipeline obtained 21 LPE exploits for about $32,936, compared with 26 confirmed 0-day LPE exploits accepted by that program in all of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: On an adapted kernelCTF environment, which is a version of the Linux kernel with reduced attack surface, our pipeline obtained 25 information leak PoCs and 21 LPE exploits. For comparison, 26 confirmed 0-day LPE exploits have been accepted by kernelCTF in 2026 at the time of writing.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI warns that, near term, a low-privileged account on an unpatched OS should be considered functionally equivalent to root for a well-resourced attacker, and says automated patch generation is essential.
key_facts.excerpt: having access to a low-privileged account on an operating system, that isn't up-to-date on its latest available patches should be considered functionally equivalent to root access for a well-resourced threat actor.

key_facts.fact: The figures are OpenAI's own and the model is not publicly available; in an early run, human review found 20 of 200 reported successes had reached root through a different 0-day than the one assigned.
key_facts.excerpt: In an early run, the exploitation stage reported 200 successful exploits. Human review found that 20 of them had reached root through a different 0-day than the one the agent had been assigned.

stories.headline: OpenAI drops NDAs with officials, pledges to cover power costs after midterm data center rebuke

key_facts.fact: On Nov 5, two days after the midterms, OpenAI published a National Community Compact and a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint; it urged policymakers to turn similar commitments into law.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI.

key_facts.fact: At future campuses it owns and operates, the only sites the compact covers, OpenAI says it will pay the full cost of its electricity and the infrastructure serving it, and provide financial assurances protecting other customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.
key_facts.excerpt: The compact sets out what communities can expect from OpenAI at future campuses that we own and operate. ... We'll pay the full cost of the electricity we use and the infrastructure needed to serve us. Before major spending begins, we'll provide financial assurances so other customers are protected if a project is delayed, reduced, or canceled.

key_facts.fact: It will not use NDAs with public officials, apart from narrow carve-outs for security information, trade secrets and competitively sensitive data, and will publish site-level water and electricity use, construction plans and independent noise studies.
key_facts.excerpt: we will not use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials, allowing only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it had been developing the commitments for months and that they were not a response to the election results; chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane said they came from discussions with residents and officials in Georgia, Ohio, Texas and other states.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said it had been developing the commitments for months and that they were not a response to the election results. ... Chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane said OpenAI developed the commitments through discussions with residents and officials in Georgia, Ohio, Texas and other states.

key_facts.fact: Voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures in all but one of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, according to Ballotpedia and CNBC.
key_facts.excerpt: Out of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures for all but one, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: WSJ reports that by Wednesday morning senior OpenAI leaders were discussing whether the results meant resetting expectations for next year's data center capacity, citing a person familiar with the conversation.
key_facts.excerpt: By Wednesday morning, senior leaders at OpenAI were discussing whether the results meant the company would have to reset expectations regarding its data center capacity next year, according to a person familiar with the conversation.

key_facts.fact: Texas, Georgia and Ohio hold more than 40% of planned US data center capacity, per Evercore ISI; OpenAI's Stargate is under construction in Texas and it plans Project Camellia in Georgia.
key_facts.excerpt: Texas, Georgia and Ohio account for more than 40% of all planned data center capacity in the U.S., according to investment bank Evercore ISI. OpenAI's Stargate is under construction in Texas and it is planning another massive data center effort—Project Camellia—in Georgia.

stories.headline: Moonshot opens Kimi K3.1 Pro weights; Ricursive's $32M Ripple-65B claims US open-coding lead

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI released the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face on Nov 4, as it had promised when it launched the model in October.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI's AI model ' Kimi K3.1 Pro ,' released on October 24, 2026, now has its 'weights' made available for free, as originally announced.

key_facts.fact: The model has 2.8 trillion total and 104 billion active parameters, a 1,048,576-token context and a 1.56 TB download, ungated.
key_facts.excerpt: 96 safetensors files totaling 1,561,293,160,568 bytes (1.56 TB). The card states MXFP4 weights and MXFP8 activations, 2.8T total parameters, 104B activated, 896 experts with 16 selected and 2 shared, a 1,048,576-token context, and text plus image input.

key_facts.fact: The license is custom, not MIT or Apache: Model-as-a-Service use needs a separate Moonshot deal once the licensee's revenue exceeds $20M in any 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Model-as-a-Service use needs a separate Moonshot agreement once the licensee's aggregate revenue exceeds $20 million in any 12 months

key_facts.fact: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview on Nov 4 under Apache 2.0: a 65-billion-parameter dense model trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens, for a stated total R&D cost of $32M. The cost and benchmarks have not been independently verified.
key_facts.excerpt: Its developer claims the top score among American open models on Terminal-Bench 2.1, with a total cost of $32 million. These figures have yet to be independently verified.

key_facts.fact: Ricursive reports 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a narrow lead over Reflection Beam (80.1), and 79.1 on SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard, but trails Meta's Muse Spark Open 44.3 to 60.0 on DeepSWE; Reflection's own comparison lists several Chinese models above Ripple's Terminal-Bench score.
key_facts.excerpt: A broader coding crown would overstate that evidence. Reflection's own published comparison lists several Chinese-developed models above Ripple's reported Terminal-Bench result.

key_facts.fact: Ripple is a general-purpose variant of the model behind Ricursive's chip-design platform; founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini helped create Google's AlphaChip, and the startup raised a $300M Series A at a $4B valuation in January.
key_facts.excerpt: Ricursive announced a $300 million Series A in January, led by Lightspeed at a $4 billion valuation, with participation from investors including Nvidia's NVentures, DST Global and Sequoia.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter's GMI Cloud endpoint prices Ripple at $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter's GMICloud endpoint charges $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Images 2.6 with GIF creation; users now make over 4B images a week

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched Images 2.6 on Nov 4 in ChatGPT and Codex across all tiers on web, desktop and mobile.
key_facts.excerpt: Images 2.6 is available today in ChatGPT, and Codex across all tiers on web, desktop, and mobile.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT can now natively generate animated GIFs from a prompt or uploaded photo, with controls for playback speed and individual frames.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT can now create GIFs using a prompt or a photo uploaded to the AI chatbot. The update, which is rolling out alongside OpenAI's new Images 2.6 model, allows you to adjust the GIF's animation speed, edit individual frames, and share it with others.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says users generate over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, up from 3 billion reported in September.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says users now generate over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, a jump from the 3 billion per week it reported in September.

key_facts.fact: Two API models launch: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare, which generates images in as little as six seconds, and Sunburst, aimed at higher quality and consistency across edits; image markup and SVG exports are also added.
key_facts.excerpt: Two new image models for developers: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst. Flare generates images in as little as six seconds. Sunburst brings higher-quality generation and greater consistency across edits. Image markup and SVG exports give you more ways to refine and use what you create.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the API models generate images 50% faster, and the ChatGPT update adds reference images.
key_facts.excerpt: Images, upgraded—introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6. Now with GIFs and reference images. Plus, two new models are coming to the API with 50% faster image generation.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: DeepMind spinout Isomorphic Labs in talks to raise ~$5B at ~$50B, with no human trials

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind, is in talks to raise about $5B at a valuation of about $50B, Bloomberg reported on Nov 4 citing people familiar; the financing has not closed and details could change.
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs, the drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind, is in talks to raise about $5bn, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The round would put the Isomorphic Labs valuation at about $50bn, according to people familiar with the matter. The financing has not closed and the details could change

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg had reported in October early talks at $40B or more; in May the company raised $2.1B in a round led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet among the other investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported in October that Isomorphic was in early talks for a round valuing it at $40bn or more, and as high as $50bn. In May, the company raised $2.1bn in a round led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet among the other investors.

key_facts.fact: The company has no drug in human trials. Hassabis said in January that first trials should start by the end of 2026; on Monday, president Max Jaderberg said its drug work was still preclinical and described the company as in its 'first innings'.
key_facts.excerpt: In January, Hassabis said Isomorphic expected to start its first clinical trials by the end of 2026, Bloomberg reported. On Monday, at Bloomberg Tech in London, Isomorphic president Max Jaderberg said its drug work was still in preclinical stages. He described the company as in its "first innings".

key_facts.fact: If the round closes, total external funding would reach about $7.7B in under two years.
key_facts.excerpt: If the $5 billion round closes, total external funding will be around $ 7.7 billion in under 2 years.

key_facts.fact: Rival Chai Discovery raised $400M at a $3.8B valuation in July, making Isomorphic's target about 13x higher.
key_facts.excerpt: Chai Discovery raised $400m at a $3.8 billion valuation in July, so Isomorphic's $50 billion valuation is some 13x higher.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: Apple cuts engineers' daily AI cap from $300 to $200; other teams could fall to $25

key_facts.fact: Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for some engineers from $300 to $200 last month and is planning further cuts to as little as $100 for some teams, Bloomberg reported on Nov 4.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, Apple quietly lowered the daily spending cap for some engineers using AI models to $200 from $300, according to people with knowledge of the change. The company is now planning further cuts for some engineering teams, potentially reducing their daily allowances to as little as $100

key_facts.fact: Many groups outside engineering already face a $100 daily cap, and Apple has considered dropping it to as little as $25 for some teams; staff can request exemptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Many groups outside of engineering already face a $100 daily cap, but Apple has considered reducing that limit to as little as $25 for some teams

key_facts.fact: Apple is asking some teams to use cheaper models or switch to on-device AI; employees have access to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other models.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is asking some teams to use less expensive models or switch to on-device AI. Employees who need a bigger budget will be able to ask executives for an increase.

key_facts.fact: Sources told Bloomberg that few workers were using their full $300 allowances, so savings may be small.
key_facts.excerpt: Gurman's sources claim that "few workers were using their full $300 daily allowances, making the previous limits unnecessarily generous," which suggests the savings obtained through the measure will be small.

key_facts.fact: Apple has also hired outside productivity consultants for some divisions, and with the AI cost cuts those reviews have fueled worries about a possible restructuring.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has also hired outside productivity consultants for some divisions. Combined with the AI cost cuts, the reviews have fueled worries about possible restructuring.

stories.headline: Brockman: OpenAI revenue run rate rose 70% in Q3, 2027 IPO possible; Claude Code's PM head joins

key_facts.fact: Speaking at a WSJ tech conference in Napa on Nov 4, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, asked whether an IPO next year was possible, said 'I think so' and added that the company wants to list when the time is right.
key_facts.excerpt: Greg Brockman, OpenAI co-founder and president, was asked at the WSJ Tech Conference held in Napa, California, whether preparations for an IPO next year were possible, and said, "I think so."

key_facts.fact: Brockman called the first half 'pretty rough' as Anthropic gained on enterprise coding, saying OpenAI was not 'even in the conversation' in coding.
key_facts.excerpt: "Q1 was pretty rough, Q2 was pretty rough. It felt like in many ways we were not even in the conversation," he said, referring to the company's position in the competition with Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: He said annualized revenue grew 70% quarter over quarter in Q3.
key_facts.excerpt: He said OpenAI recorded 70% quarterly growth in annualized revenue, while its enterprise business surged during the period.

key_facts.fact: Brockman called it a 'revenue inflection' driven by the enterprise business, helped by the release of GPT-5.6 Sol and ChatGPT Work.
key_facts.excerpt: he said revenue rose sharply in the third quarter, helped by the release of the AI model "GPT-5.6 Sol" and the enterprise service "ChatGPT Work." Brockman called it "an amazing revenue inflection point."

key_facts.fact: Brockman said OpenAI is now 'somewhere around majority enterprise', meaning business customers generate more than half of revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: He said OpenAI recorded 70% quarterly growth in annualized revenue, while its enterprise business surged during the period. ... Now we are somewhere around majority enterprise.

key_facts.fact: He disclosed expanded work with JPMorgan, particularly on cyber; Anthropic also has a cyber deal with the bank.
key_facts.excerpt: Oh yea, and he broke some news that OpenAI is expanding its work with JP Morgan, particularly on stuff like cyber. Anthropic also has a deal to work with JP Morgan on cyber

key_facts.fact: Cat Wu announced on the evening of Nov 4 (US time) that she is joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products.
key_facts.excerpt: Some news: I'm joining OpenAI to lead product management for Core Products!

key_facts.fact: Wu left Anthropic last week after two years as Head of Product for Claude Code, Business Insider reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Cat Wu, who left Anthropic last week after becoming one of the company's highest-profile product managers, is joining OpenAI. (Techmeme summary: Wu was the Head of Product for Claude Code for two years.)
